title: Qatayef Asafiri with Ashta Cream and Orange Blossom Syrup
summary: Delicate one-sided pancakes folded into cones and filled with a silky rose-scented cream, dipped in pistachios and finished with orange blossom syrup.
equipment: baking tray lined with baking paper

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Cook
steps.text: Whisk 240 ml milk, 240 ml double cream and 2 tbsp cornflour over low heat until dissolved, then whisk in 2 tbsp plain flour for 1 min, followed by 1 tbsp sugar and 55 g cream cheese until smooth.

steps.title: Thicken
steps.text: Raise the heat, stirring constantly to a boil, and boil about 2 min until thick like custard, then stir in 1 tsp rose water, press cling film onto the surface and cool completely, about 1 h, before chilling.

steps.title: Batter
steps.text: Whisk 65 g plain flour, 20 g semolina, 13 g sugar, ¼ tsp yeast, ⅛ tsp salt and 160 ml warm water, then cover and leave 1.5-2 h until bubbly and foamy.

steps.title: Syrup
steps.text: Simmer 200 g sugar with 120 ml water about 8 min until it coats a spoon, then stir in 2 tbsp orange blossom water and 1 tsp lemon juice, simmer 30 s and cool.

steps.title: Cook
steps.text: Blend ⅛ tsp bicarbonate of soda into the batter, pour about 1.5 tbsp per pancake into a hot non-stick pan and cook on one side only, 1-2 min, until the surface is covered in holes; do not flip.

steps.title: Fold
steps.text: While still warm, fold each pancake in half and press the edges together partway to form an open cone.

steps.title: Fill
steps.text: Pipe or spoon the chilled ashta into the opening, dip the exposed cream in 2 tbsp chopped pistachios, and serve chilled with the syrup drizzled over or on the side.

tips: Cook the pancakes on one side only, waiting until the surface is full of small holes and feels dry before moving them.
Fold and fill the pancakes while they're still warm and pliable so they hold their cone shape.
Chill the ashta thoroughly before piping so it holds its shape neatly inside each pancake.
safety: Don't taste the raw dough or batter: raw flour and raw egg aren't safe to eat until baked.
storage: Make the ashta and batter ahead and keep them chilled separately, but fill and serve the pancakes fresh, keeping any already filled for no more than a day in the fridge.
